data.title: Live updates: August's strong jobs numbers put rate cut in doubt; Trump signs beef deal
data.description:
The U.S. economy added 162,000 jobs last month, a stronger-than-expected showing. And now President Trump wants to see interest rates dropped, threatening to cut off trade with several countries if the Federal Reserve doesn’t budge at its September meeting.

“Without the United States agreeing to allow them their big surpluses, and we could stop that immediately, they would no longer be considered financially ELITE!” he wrote on Truth Social. “LOWER THE RATE OR I’LL STOP TRADING WITH COUNTRIES WITH WHICH WE HAVE A DEFICIT.”

On Friday afternoon, Trump signed an executive order allowing tariff-free imported beef, coming from Brazil and Argentina, among other places, as his administration works to alleviate stubbornly high prices.

The judge in the Lindsay Clancy murder case announced Friday that he was declaring a mistrial after jurors were unable to reach a unanimous verdict. However, when defense attorney Kevin Reddington requested an immediate stay of the declaration, the judge gave the defense one hour to appeal.

North Carolina is set to begin mailing general election absentee ballots Friday, even as the Trump administration has moved to restrict voting by mail.

The administration is appealing a federal judge’s ruling that stops it from moving forward with voting restrictions established by executive order for at least for one more week. The Justice Department asked the Supreme Court on Thursday to lift the block.

Trump had a policy meeting and will sign an executive order Friday before heading to New Jersey for the holiday weekend.

Follow along live below.

data.title: Trump signs controversial beef deal with Brazil, Argentina
data.description:
President Trump said Friday that tariff-free imported beef will be coming from Brazil and Argentina, among other places, as his administration works to alleviate stubbornly high prices.

“It’s coming from Argentina. It’s coming from Brazil,” Trump said at an Oval Office event surrounded by ranchers and farmers. “It’s coming from a couple of other places. We have our inspectors down. It’s very clean. It’s very good.”

Trump announced last month that the U.S. would be pausing tariffs on 300,000 metric tons of beef for 90 days to be sold at a 25 percent discount below market price. The president said it would lower costs for Americans while allowing for ranchers to build up their herds.

The announcement was quickly criticized by the cattle industry and GOP lawmakers who said that lowering prices for Americans shouldn’t come at the cost of U.S. ranchers.

“We’re doing it in a very limited fashion because our ranchers can handle it, but our ranchers really needed a little bit of help, and our ranchers want the prices to be down, too,” Trump said.

The White House further defended the decision after a report that a Brazilian billionaire influenced it. The Wall Street Journal reported Monday that Trump met with Joesley Batisa, who shares control of JBS, the world’s largest meatpacker, a day before the announcement.

Batista and his brother Wesley Batista were fined in 2020 by the Justice Department over charges that they violated the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act by using funds obtained through a bribery scheme to expand operations in the U.S.

The tariff pause also follows the unrelated recall of nearly 30,000 pounds of Argentinian beef that had been distributed in Texas and Florida.

Trump was behind the Resolute Desk Friday to sign two executive orders, one that allows ranchers and farmers to butcher, process, package and sell their own products and another that requires country-of-origin labeling across all foreign beef.

Trump said the big four processors in the U.S. beef sector — Tyson Foods, JBS S.A., Cargill and National Beef Packing Co. — have a “monopoly” on the industry.

“I’ve heard all about it. I’ve been listening to it… and they say they’re a very nasty group, very difficult to deal with,” he said of the processors. “And they cost our farmers a lot of money, and they cost our ranchers a lot of money, and they cost the public a lot of money in grief, and we’re not going to let it happen any longer.”

When asked about the timeline on the country-of-origin labeling, Trump said he would need to go through Capitol Hill.

“We’re putting it in front of Congress right away,” he said. “It should be no problem.”

data.title: Supreme Court sides with GOP in fight over TV ad rates; Jackson dissents
data.description:
The Supreme Court on Friday lifted a ruling that prevented party committees from accessing cheaper advertising rates in the lead-up to November’s elections, siding with Republicans, for now, in an emergency case that drew staunch Democratic opposition.

Federal law mandates that broadcast stations offer their lowest available rate in the 60 days preceding a general election. Everyone agrees candidates get the discount, but whether political parties and joint fundraising committees can, too, has come under question.

The court appeared to split 8-1, though the justices don’t have to disclose their votes in emergency decisions publicly. The majority said that federal courts had no authority yet to intervene in the dispute.

Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson, the court’s junior liberal justice, publicly dissented.

Republicans’ Senate and House campaign arms — boasting a cash advantage and backed by the Trump administration — brought the fight to the Supreme Court after Democrats sued to stop them from accessing the cheaper rate.

Democrats won before the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 4th Circuit. In a 2-1 decision, the panel ruled the Federal Communications Commission’s (FCC) notice asserting the committees could enjoy the discount wasn’t legal.

In their Supreme Court filings, Republicans largely centered their case on the notion that the judges had no authority to get involved, describing the notice as a “staff-level guidance document.”

“The decision opens the floodgates, allowing challenges to staff decisions of the FCC and other agencies in parallel tracks before the Commission and courts,” they wrote in court filings.

Republicans’ emergency appeal garnered support from the Trump administration, which similarly told the high court the lower courts had no authority.

“The challengers claim, and the court of appeals agreed, that the notice injures them by making it cheaper for their opponents to run campaign advertisements,” Solicitor General D. John Sauer wrote to the justices. “But the notice does not grant favored treatment to one side or the other; instead, the notice’s interpretation offers the same benefit to all sides”

Democrats insisted to the justices the lower courts acted properly and had power to intervene.

“On both reviewability and the merits, Applicants and the United States want to talk about everything except the text of the directly pertinent statutes. That is because on both questions, the text directly supports Candidates,” they wrote in court filings.

data.title: 4 House Democrats heading to Dallas for RNC counterprogramming
data.description:
Four House Democrats are headed to Dallas next week as the Republican National Committee holds a first-of-its-kind midterm convention, House leadership announced on Friday. 

Reps. Robert Garcia, (D-Calif.), Jason Crow (D-Colo.), Madeleine Dean (D-Pa.) and Sydney Kamlager-Dove (D-Calif.) make up the delegation, which will partner with local leaders and the Texas Democratic Party on the ground. 

“While swing seat House Republicans try to hide from their record of raising costs on working families, gutting Medicaid to fund tax breaks for billionaire donors and supporting a reckless war of choice in Iran, House Democrats will be present to hold them accountable,” House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-N.Y.) said in a release. 

Jeffries accused MAGA extremists of “partying with their super rich donors in Dallas” as Americans feel the sting of high prices.

“Americans are being crushed by rising costs. Republicans don’t care—they’re in Dallas, celebrating an out of touch President whose tariffs and wars are making things worse. We’re going to hold them accountable,” Crow said on X.

The Democrats’ Texas visit acts as a counterprogramming to the RNC’s convention, which is aimed at highlighting Republican candidates and energizing the party’s voters ahead of the high-stakes midterm election. Vice President Vance is giving a speech the first night, and President Trump is set to deliver the closing-night keynote address. 

The Dallas-based event comes as Republicans fight to hold on to the Texas Senate seat up for grabs in November, and as both parties battle over a handful of highly competitive House seats after GOP-friendly redistricting reshaped the state’s congressional maps last year.

data.title: Virginia Democrat says DOJ wiretapped phone calls with state Senate leader
data.description:
Rep. Suhas Subramanyam (D-Va.) said Thursday that the FBI and Justice Department (DOJ) informed him they had wiretapped his past phone conversations with a Virginia state lawmaker.

Subramanyam’s office shared photos of two letters he said he received from the agencies, dated from July and August, notifying him they monitored some of his calls with Virginia state Senate President Pro Tempore Louise Lucas (D).

The representative slammed this action as “deeply concerning” in his Thursday statement, accusing the Trump administration of trying to intimidate Democrats.

A federal judge authorized the phone call interception in April, according to the letters. A month later, federal agents conducted a search of Lucas’ office and a cannabis dispensary she co-owned as part of this investigation. The state legislator has denied any wrongdoing and claimed the federal probe was politically motivated. 

Subramanyam’s statement described called the timing of the phone tapping and investigation into the Virginia state senate leader “extremely suspicious.”

He noted the probe occurred within the same period Virginia Democrats were pushing for a redistricting referendum — an effort that Lucas championed.

The Virginia representative also pointed to his role on the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform as a potential reason for the agencies’ scrutiny, noting he and other Democrats were demanding answers from the DOJ at the time over its handling of the investigation into late convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

“This should concern anyone who believes in a real Department of Justice that serves the American people and not a singular president,” Subramanyam said.

“If this surveillance was done to scare us and to get Democrats to stop pushing back against [President] Trump’s political overreach, they are mistaken,” he continued. “We will not back down. We will continue our investigations into this President and his corrupt administration.”  

The Hill has reached out to the DOJ and Lucas for comment. The FBI declined to comment.

data.title: Pennsylvania Democrat blasts Fetterman as 'lazy trust fund baby'
data.description:
Rep. Brandan Boyle (D-Pa.) slammed his fellow Pennsylvania Democrat Sen. John Fetterman (D-Pa.) Thursday, calling him a “lazy trust fund baby” following reports that Fetterman has been neglecting his duties as a Senator.

“John Fetterman is a disgrace,” the congressman said in a post on social platform X. “Our state deserves better than a lazy trust fund baby who is too lazy to do the job.” Fetterman has said that his parents financially supported him into his forties.

The statement was sparked by a Wall Street Journal report that alleged the senator avoided meeting with three disabled service members, later opting to do an interview with Fox News on Israel and the war in Iran in seemingly good health.

He also reportedly attempted to dodge a similar meeting with the Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia who grew concerned over Medicaid funding cuts in last year’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBA).

At the time, Fetterman received backlash from Boyle for saying that the act’s long voting process caused him to miss “our entire trip to the beach.”

“I will do whatever it takes, stay up for 48 straight hours, 72 straight hours, do whatever it takes to block this bill from becoming law,” Boyle said at the time. “And that should be the attitude, frankly, of every Democratic member of the House and Senate.”

The report noted that for the past year, Fetterman attended 26 of the 31 full hearings for his assigned committees but did not speak in 20 of them which sparked outrage from other Pennsylvania Democrats. 

“There is a lot I could say about this report of John Fetterman’s pathetic behavior as a Senator,” Rep. Chris Deluzio (D-Pa.) said on X Thursday. “But between the laziness, disrespect, and willingness to carry water for a foreign government, it shows us something we already know: this man has no sense of duty.”

“He is not up for the high office he was elected to — and we in Pennsylvania will do something about it in 2028,” he added.

Democratic National Committee Vice Chair and Pennsylvania state Rep. Malcolm Kenyatta (D) told News Nation on Sunday that Fetterman “is somebody who has spent the past few years not doing his job. He is a part-time senator, full-time commentator on Fox News.”

In a separate Friday statement, Kenyetta said, “2028 can’t come soon enough” and that Fetterman “barely showed up as LG and is constantly MIA as our Senator.”

data.title: Former Kentucky Gov. Matt Bevin arrested on film set
data.description:
Former Kentucky Gov. Matt Bevin (R) was arrested Thursday at a movie set over an outstanding warrant in his divorce and child support case.

Bevin was booked into a Louisville jail that evening after the Bourbon County Sheriff’s Office arrested Bevin in Paris, Ky., during the filming of a Christmas movie.

The former governor was playing a “featured extra” in the film and was talking to the film’s lead actor when deputies arrived, property owner Jessica Mohr told Kentucky Public Radio, which first reported the arrest.

“The sheriff showed up and was asking some people if they’d seen his picture, and a young man was like, ‘I think that gentleman’s inside,’” Mohr said. “And yeah, he was arrested.”

Bourbon County Sheriff Tony Asbury confirmed in a press release that he had an active warrant for Bevin’s arrest and that his office had received a tip that the former governor was involved in a film project at the horse farm estate.

“The Bourbon County Sheriff’s Office contacted Former Governor Bevin at the location reported and he was taken into custody shortly after and lodged into the Bourbon-Nicholas County Region Detention Center without any issues as Bevin was very cooperative,” Asbury said in a statement.

The warrant was issued after Jefferson Family Court Judge Angela Johnson found Bevin in contempt for failing to turn over financial documents in a case involving his ex-wife, Glenna Bevin.

Johnson sentenced him in June to 60 days in jail and a $500 fine. He was issued an earlier warrant for failing to appear for a May court hearing, which he claimed he could not make because a boulder crashed into his home in Maine.

Matt Bevin, who served as governor from 2015 to 2019, lost in his reelection bid to current Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear (D). His running mate at the time, Ralph Alvarado, is currently the Republican candidate in Kentucky’s 6th Congressional District to replace Rep. Andy Barr (R-Ky.), who is running for Senate.

“No one who thought it was a good idea to run alongside Matt Bevin should represent the families of Kentucky’s Sixth Congressional District,” the Kentucky Democratic Party said in a statement.

A spokesperson for Alvarado said Bevin should be held responsible for failing to follow the court’s orders.

“Court orders are not optional, and everyone should comply with the court’s directive,” spokesperson Andrew Westberry told The Hill. “Failure to do so has consequences.”

data.title: Publix, Walmart, other grocers under investigation over beef prices
data.description:
TAMPA, Fla. (WFLA) — The Department of Justice (DOJ) is expanding its investigation into beef affordability in the U.S. to include eight of the largest grocers in the country.

Earlier this week, the DOJ posted to social platform X that its Antitrust Division sent letters to these eight grocers over the retail price of beef:

  • Kroger
  • Publix
  • Walmart
  • Albertsons
  • Aldi
  • Ahold Delhaize USA
  • Costco
  • Amazon

“Beef prices are a critical concern to Americans, and a priority for this Justice Department,” the department wrote.

Newsweek reported that the letters were dated in July and sought data in the companies’ records regarding retail sales and prices, costs and margins for beef products, their analyses of market trends and other information related to beef.

According to Reuters, the Antitrust Division began investigating meat packers after President Trump accused them of manipulating beef prices.

Tyson Foods, for example, settled a class action lawsuit earlier this year for $82.5 million after grocers accused the business of restricting supply to inflate U.S. beef prices.

Beef prices have been another issue plaguing the Trump administration, with the president saying in August that he would pause beef import tariffs to bring cheaper meat into the market.

“As we work to rebuild this herd and help our ranchers, for the next 90 days, the United States will allow up to 300,000 metric tons of product for ground beef to be imported with no out of quota tariff,” Trump wrote Aug. 21 on Truth Social.

“We have a commitment that this beef will be sold at 25 percent below current market prices. This deal will reduce prices for Americans while giving space for our Great American Beef Herd to grow again,” he added at the time.

This has riled American beef herders and other Republican lawmakers who pushed against the plan, with Sen. Thom Tillis (R-N.C.) calling it a mistake.

“If you think that providing subsidized beef for some period of time is going to make farmers happy and prices go down on a systemic basis, you’re wrong,” Tillis said. “It doesn’t happen.”

Publix and Walmart did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

data.title: Witkoff, Kushner to visit Russia, Ukraine in effort to jumpstart peace talks
data.description:
Two top U.S. envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, will travel to Russia and Ukraine this weekend in an effort to restart peace negotiations between the two countries, according to multiple reports. 

Witkoff and Kushner — Trump’s special envoy and son-in-law, respectively — will first meet with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow on Saturday, The New York Times reported.

The duo will then travel to Kyiv on Sunday to meet with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, a Ukrainian source with knowledge of these plans confirmed to The Hill’s broadcast partner, NewsNation. 

Zelensky also confirmed the U.S. delegation’s trip to Kyiv in a statement shared on social media Friday afternoon, citing details confirmed by Trump’s team. 

The Ukrainian leader confirmed his military will hold off launching air strikes during this trip “so that the negotiators can arrive safely.”

“Our goal is to make the visit and the talks with the U.S. side as constructive and substantive as possible,” Zelensky wrote. “We need to look for real options for how to move this war toward an end. We will see what proposals Steve and Jared bring and what they are told in Moscow in response.”

The details of these peace talks have not been disclosed. The Hill has reached out to the White House for comment. 

The trip will mark the first trip to the Ukrainian capital for both Witkoff and Kushner. Both men have made several visits to Moscow during this conflict. It also follows CIA Director John Ratcliffe’s unannounced visit to Moscow last week. 

Russian state-run news agency TASS reported Friday that the U.S. envoys planned to travel to the country “soon,” citing unnamed sources.

Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said in a Friday statement shared by TASS that there are no set conditions yet to reach a peace agreement with Ukraine.

“Unfortunately, there are no specific prerequisites yet. Work continues and communication is ongoing,” Peskov added, according to the state-run outlet. 

These reported travel plans come amid escalating attacks in the yearslong dispute between these two countries, as both sides reject each other’s demands and Putin continues to push Ukraine to give up a large portion of its territory.

Moscow has launched a near-continuous attack on Kyiv for the past eight days, striking buildings, warehouses and the central headquarters for Ukraine’s security service. Ukraine’s military has responded with long-range attacks on Russian oil storage and refining facilities.

data.title: Watch live: Trump to sign beef-related executive order after easing tariffs
data.description:
President Trump is set to sign an executive order Friday related to the beef industry, according to the White House.

Trump announced last month that the U.S. would pause higher tariffs on ground beef imports for 90 days, allowing up to 300,000 metric tons to enter the country without the higher “out-of-quota” tariff rate.

Trump said the move would help lower costs for consumers while giving the administration time to rebuild the U.S. cattle herd and support ranchers.

The plan has come under heavy criticism from Republicans and ranchers alike.

The signing is scheduled to begin at 1:30 p.m. EDT.
